questions.chapter: Statics of Particles and Rigid Bodies
questions.text: State and explain the fundamental principles of Newtonian mechanics and the principle of transmissibility with its limitations. State the equations of static equilibrium for 2D and 3D force systems acting on rigid bodies.

questions.chapter: Statics of Particles and Rigid Bodies
questions.text: State and prove Varignon's Theorem of moments.

questions.chapter: Distributed Forces, Centroid and Moment of Inertia
questions.text: State and prove the Parallel Axis Theorem for area moment of inertia ($I = I_G + A d^2$).

questions.chapter: Distributed Forces, Centroid and Moment of Inertia
questions.text: Determine the centroid $(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$, moment of inertia ($I_{xx}, I_{yy}$), and radius of gyration ($r_x, r_y$) of a standard composite structural section (T-section, I-section, angle section, or parabolic shaded area) about centroidal axes.
Derive the differential relationship between distributed load $w(x)$, shear force $V(x)$, and bending moment $M(x)$: $\frac{dV}{dx} = -w(x)$ and $\frac{dM}{dx} = V(x)$.

For a given loaded beam or frame carrying concentrated point loads, uniformly distributed loads (UDL), and applied couples, calculate support reactions and draw the Axial Force Diagram (AFD), Shear Force Diagram (SFD), and Bending Moment Diagram (BMD). Locate points of contraflexure and determine maximum bending moment.

Compute the forces developed in specified members of a pin-jointed plane truss (Warren truss, Pratt truss) using the Method of Joints and the Method of Sections. Indicate whether each member is in tension or compression.
Define angle of friction, angle of repose, and cone of friction. Explain the conditions for sliding versus tipping (overturning) of a rectangular block resting on an inclined plane.

A uniform ladder of length $L$ and weight $W$ leans against a vertical wall and horizontal floor with friction. Determine the minimum coefficient of friction or maximum inclination angle to prevent slipping when a person ascends the ladder.

The acceleration of a particle moving rectilinearly is defined by the relation $a = -10 x^{-2}$ (or $a = -kv$ or $a = 3t$). If the particle starts with specified initial conditions, determine its velocity, position, and total distance traveled.

A projectile is launched from an initial elevation with velocity $v_0$ at an angle $\theta$ to the horizontal. Derive expressions for maximum height $H_{\max}$, horizontal range $R$, and time of flight $T$, and determine its velocity and strike angle on an inclined target.

State and prove the Work-Energy Principle for a particle ($T_1 + U_{1-2} = T_2$). State and explain the principle of conservation of mechanical energy for a system of connected particles with springs and gravity.

State the Principle of Linear Impulse and Momentum. Explain direct central and oblique impact between two bodies with coefficient of restitution $e = \frac{v_2' - v_1'}{v_1 - v_2}$ and solve an impact problem.

Define angular momentum of a particle. Prove that the rate of change of angular momentum of a particle about a fixed point equals the sum of moments of external forces acting on it ($\sum M_O = \dot{H}_O$).

State D'Alembert's Principle for rigid bodies. Derive equations of planar motion for a rigid body undergoing general plane motion, showing decomposition into translational motion of center of mass ($F = ma_G$) and rotational motion about center of mass ($M_G = I_G \alpha$).
Explain the analysis of flexible cables supporting concentrated and uniformly distributed loads. Derive the cable tension and profile equations for parabolic and catenary cables.
